slides.say: A O B is a sector of a circle with center O and a radius of two centimeters. Based on this and the figure, what is the area of the shaded region, in square centimeters?
at: A O B is a sector

slides.say: The shaded region is the sector, minus the right triangle inside it. So shaded equals sector minus triangle. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, by estimating the choices, and then with a partial calculation.

slides: Let's start with an estimate, after one small calculation. We'll find the triangle's area first. Then we'll estimate the sector, and compare the choices.

slides.say: The triangle has a right angle and an angle of forty-five degrees. So its third angle is forty-five too, and its legs are equal. The hypotenuse is the radius, two. By Pythagoras, the two equal legs squared add up to four. So each leg squared is two.

The legs are equal, so their product is also two. The triangle's area is that product divided by two. Two divided by two is one. Now the sector. Forty-five degrees is one eighth of a full circle. The whole circle has area four pi, so this sector is pi over two.
at: Two divided by two is one
this sector is pi over two

slides.say: For this estimate, use these bounds for pi: more than three, and less than three point two. We need closer bounds here because the choices are close in size. Half of pi is therefore between one point five and one point six. Take away the triangle's area, one. The shaded area is between zero point five and zero point six.
at: more than three, and less than three point two
between zero point five and zero point six

slides.say: Choice number one is four minus pi. Pi is less than three point two, so four minus pi is more than zero point eight. Our area is less than zero point six. So choice number one is too big, and it's out.

Choice number three is pi over root two. Root two is less than two, so dividing pi by root two gives more than dividing pi by two. That's more than one point five, much bigger than our area. So choice number three is out. Choice numbers two and four are left.
[pause] Two choices are left. Now let's estimate their size. Pi is a bit more than three, and less than four.
at: Pi is a bit more than three

slides.say: Look at choice number two. Inside the bracket, we have pi over two, minus two. Pi is less than four, so pi over two is less than four over two, which is two.
If we take two away from something less than two, we get a negative number. And half of a negative number is still negative. So choice number two is a negative number.
But an area can't be negative, so choice number two is out. The exam won't write minus five. It hides the minus behind the pi, and an estimate shows it at once.
at: But an area can't be negative
so choice number two is out

slides.say: Three choices are out, so choice number four is our answer.
at: so choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now a second way, the math way, for whoever wants to calculate. Even then, we don't have to calculate everything. Let's find only the sector.
What part of the circle is the sector? Think of a pizza. If we cut it into four slices, each slice has ninety degrees. If we cut it into eight, each slice has forty-five degrees.
at: If we cut it into eight

slides.say: Our angle is forty-five degrees, so the sector is one of eight equal slices. It's one eighth of the circle.
The area of the circle is pi r squared. The radius is two, and two squared is four, so the circle is four pi. One eighth of four pi is four pi over eight, which is pi over two.

The shaded area is pi over two, minus the triangle's area. We found that the triangle's area is one. So the result is pi over two minus one. Choice number four matches both pieces, not just the way the expression looks.

Choice number two has a half outside its whole bracket. It gives pi over four minus one, not pi over two minus one. So it's out. We compare the actual values of the pieces, not just whether a minus sign is written. Choice number four again.
This is a partial calculation: find a useful piece, then look at the choices. A piece can rule choices out, but the answer still has to fit the whole shaded area. I'll see you in the next question.
